subject: Cohesive uplift & credit exchange - mid-contract expansion
messages:
From: Anna Kapoor <anna@datawave.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <purchasing@datawave.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract expansion options

Hi Dylan,

We're seeing higher-than-expected Q3 usage and want to add ~150k tokens/month effective immediately. We prefer to avoid a separate monthly invoice if possible — exploring options to either (a) top up now pro-rated and pay monthly, or (b) annualize the add-on and co-term it to our existing contract renewal in 60 days.

Key asks:
- Target blended uplift discount if we annualize (benchmark: 10-20%)
- Confirmation that added capacity can be co-termed to our Feb 2028 renewal
- Any impacts to SLA/latency when we provision this additional capacity

Can you share a quick options matrix + ballpark pricing?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Kapoor
Head of Platform
DataWave Analytics
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kapoor <anna@datawave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract expansion options

Hi Anna — thanks for the details. Short answer: both paths are feasible. I attached a short quote (DataWave_uplift_quote_v1.pdf) and a one-page summary. High-level options: 

1) Immediate top-up (pro-rated monthly):
   - Provision + bill pro-rata for remainder of month, then monthly usage invoices.
   - No long-term credit; preserves flexibility.
   - No change to SLA; we route requests to your existing Dedicated pool.

2) Annualize (voucher-style credits, co-term to Feb 2028):
   - You commit to the uplift as an annual add-on and receive a blended discount. For an uplift of ~150k tokens/mo, I can propose a 10% discount baseline with a 12%/13% escalation if you accelerate to a 12-month prepay.
   - We can apply a voucher that smooths billing and co-terms to Feb 2028; a pro-rata true-up will occur at co-term.

To move faster, I can propose an initial commercial offer: 12% blended discount, voucher-based annualization, immediate provisioning, and a written mutual action plan (MAP). That maintains your latency SLO and keeps billing simple.

Attaching: DataWave_uplift_quote_v1.pdf (quote), and will follow up with an uplift matrix.

Would you be open to the 12% as a starting point? If legal needs different invoicing, we can adjust.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Expansion
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: DataWave_uplift_quote_v1.pdf (pdf, 1 page)
From: Anna Kapoor <anna@datawave.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <purchasing@datawave.ai>, Legal <legal@datawave.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract expansion options

Dylan — appreciate the fast reply and the quote. A couple notes from our side after an internal review: 

- We'd prefer a single annualized amendment to avoid multiple invoices — simplifies PO management.
- Given our budget window, we'd need a ~18% blended discount to justify committing the uplift as an annual add-on.
- We can accept a pro-rata true-up at co-term but need clarity on the true-up formula (monthly usage vs. committed units).
- SLA is a must; can you confirm Redwood will keep our existing latency SLA on the uplifted capacity (we need <250ms p95 for production traffic).

If you can come back with a firm 15%–18% band (final number contingent on approvals) plus the amendment language for co-terming and true-up calculation, I'll loop legal.

Thanks,
Anna

> Hi Anna — thanks for the details. Short answer: both paths are feasible. I attached a short quote...
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kapoor <anna@datawave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cohesive uplift & credit exchange - mid-contract expansion

Thanks for the context, Anna — looping in Monica (CS) and Jordan (renewals) so we can align on SLA and legal wording. Monica: can you confirm operational impact for a +150k token/mo uplift in the Dedicated pool? Jordan: I'll need a clean amendment template to bound the co-term / true-up clauses.

Commercial suggestion from my side to bridge toward Anna's ask: 
- Offer: 14% blended discount applied to the annualized uplift (12-month voucher).
- Concession path: escalate to 16% if DataWave signs the amendment and pre-pays 6 months up front; 18% would require full 12-month prepay.
- True-up method: monthly billed usage vs. committed units; at co-term we net billed usage against committed units and issue credit or invoice for the difference. Formula and example to be included in the amendment.
- SLA: Redwood confirms no change to your existing latency SLO (<250ms p95) as long as traffic stays within the Dedicated pool thresholds. Any burst beyond reserved throughput switches to burst capacity billing (documented).

I'm attaching a short uplift matrix (redwood_uplift_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a draft MAP (mutual_action_plan.docx) that lays out signoffs, legal review timeline, and billing steps.

Next steps I propose:
1) We aim for a 14% baseline and let DataWave choose pre-pay tier if they want deeper discount.
2) Jordan to send amendment template + true-up example.
3) Anna to confirm preferred concession path (14% baseline vs. 16% 6mo prepay vs. 18% 12mo prepay).

Anna — are you ok to put the baseline 14% to legal for initial review? If so I will prepare a DocuSign envelope and the MAP.

Thanks,
Dylan

--

- Push a 14% baseline to legal as a starting position; procurement will review pre-pay options this afternoon.
- Legal asked that the amendment explicitly show the true-up worked example (you mentioned you'd include one).
- Please include the DocuSign link when you have the package ready; we need to track signoff and PO issuance timelines.

Assuming legal approves the amendment language and the true-up example matches the MAP, procurement expects to sign within 3 business days. We'll confirm whether we take the 6mo pre-pay (for 16%) or the annual pre-pay (for 18%) after an internal budget pass.

Appreciate the quick coordination.
